blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Building a useful budget is less about precision and more about honesty. A budget that looks impressive on a slide but that nobody in the operation believes is a piece of theatre. A budget that is slightly conservative, widely agreed, and visibly linked to real decisions becomes a working tool.

Good budgets are built with the teams that will live inside them, not imposed from finance. They include assumptions, clearly written down, so that when reality moves, the forecast can be updated without rewriting the story from scratch.

By the end of the year, a healthy company will have missed its budget in some places and beaten it in others — and will have learned enough from the variances to make next year's budget tighter. Budgets are learning tools. Companies that treat them as punishment miss the whole point.

items.q: According to the text, a useful budget depends more on…
items.why: "less about precision and more about honesty" — a honestidade pesa mais que a precisão.

items.q: Why should assumptions be written down clearly?
options: So finance can impose them on the teams
So the budget looks more impressive
So nobody has to agree on the numbers
So the forecast can be updated when reality moves
items.why: "so that when reality moves, the forecast can be updated without rewriting the story from scratch."

items.q: What does the text say a healthy company will have done by the end of the year?
options: Hit its budget in every department
Missed its budget in some places and beaten it in others
items.why: "will have missed its budget in some places and beaten it in others."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A missed budget is a chance to learn.
Teams should help build the budgets they work under.
A budget nobody believes is still valuable if the numbers are precise.
Assumptions should be recorded, not just totals.
items.why: Inferência: o texto chama de "theatre" o orçamento em que ninguém acredita — precisão sozinha não o salva.

items.q: Calling budgets "learning tools" suggests that variances should be treated as…
options: information that makes next year's budget better
proof that the budget was useless
evidence to punish the teams responsible
numbers to be hidden from finance
items.why: Inferência: se o orçamento é ferramenta de aprendizado, a variação ensina — daí "treat them as punishment miss the whole point".

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conduzindo o workshop de orçamento. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before anyone gives me a single number, I want to be clear about what we're doing here. We are not building a budget to impress the board. We are building one that the three of you actually believe in.

So here is the rule for today. Every figure you put on the sheet comes with the assumption behind it, written down next to it. If you tell me sales will grow eight per cent, I want to know why — which contracts, which prices, which volumes. When one of those assumptions turns out to be wrong in June, and one of them will, we open the sheet, change that line, and move on. We do not rewrite the whole story.

And please, be honest, not heroic. A budget that is slightly conservative and widely agreed is worth far more to me than an ambitious one that quietly falls apart by the second quarter.

By December, I promise you, we will have missed some of these lines and beaten others. That is fine. What matters is that by then we will have learned enough from the gaps to make next year sharper. Nobody in this room gets punished for an honest miss. People get into trouble for hiding one.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James say the budget is NOT for?
options: Helping the teams plan their year
items.why: "We are not building a budget to impress the board."

items.q: What is the rule James sets for the day?
options: No department may grow faster than eight per cent
Only conservative numbers are allowed on the sheet
Every figure must come with the assumption behind it, written down
Every figure must be approved by finance first
items.why: "Every figure you put on the sheet comes with the assumption behind it, written down next to it."

items.q: What does James want the team to do when an assumption turns out wrong in June?
options: Open the sheet, change that line, and move on
items.why: "we open the sheet, change that line, and move on. We do not rewrite the whole story."

items.q: What does "be honest, not heroic" most likely mean here?
options: Promise realistic numbers rather than flattering ones
Report only the good news to James
Set brave targets to motivate the team
items.why: Inferência: ele prefere o conservador e acordado ao ambicioso que desaba — honesto vale mais que heroico.

items.q: What can you infer James most fears from his team?
options: Hiding a miss instead of admitting it
items.why: Inferência: "Nobody gets punished for an honest miss. People get into trouble for hiding one."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A budget nobody believes is just a piece of theatre." Here, theatre means…
options: a place where plays are performed
an empty show with no real substance
items.why: Theatre = teatro, no sentido de encenação vazia — parece algo, mas ninguém acredita.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every figure rests on an ___ we should write down, such as the price of sugar next quarter."
items.why: Assumption = premissa: aquilo que se supõe verdadeiro por trás de um número.

items.q: "We prefer a slightly conservative forecast to an ambitious one." Conservative here means…
items.why: Conservative = conservador, prudente: não exagera nas projeções.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ between the plan and the actual result taught us how our costs really behave."
items.why: Variance = variação: a diferença entre o previsto e o realizado.

items.q: "Good budgets are built with the teams, not imposed from finance." To impose means to…
options: force on someone without their agreement
items.why: To impose = impor: obrigar de cima, sem construir junto com quem vai usar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de orçamento e previsão. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Finance still has to sign off on the final budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two department heads pushed back on the revenue target." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's revisit these assumptions in June when we have real data." To revisit them means to…
options: look at them again to update them
items.why: Revisit = revisitar: voltar a examinar algo para atualizá-lo.

items.q: "The team agreed the plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não foi levado.

items.q: "Trimming the stationery budget won't move the needle on our margin." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não faz.
